column2: Brahma is the sleeping of men; hence he is remembered as Narayana. Dividing himself threefold, the whole proceeds.
He creates, devours and sustains, himself by the three. First, as Hiranyagarbha, the lord himself appeared.
He is primal and self-controlled, and because of being unborn he is remembered as Aja. Hence in the Puranas he is called Hiranyagarbha.
The time of the Self-born, when he withdraws, at the front of the letters (?), cannot be counted even in hundreds of Manu-years.
Counted by kalpas, Brahma's half-life (parardha) is remembered; of the same length is his other time, at whose end he awakens.
The thousands of crores of years that have passed in kalpas, and as many that remain thereafter —
the kalpa that is now proceeding by itself is the Varaha; understand it. The first of them, the kalpa now current,
when a thousand yugas are complete, is to be ruled by kings.
Creating night again, Brahma, the god of gods, created moonlight, men's selves, nectar and the ancestors.
Then again, cleansing chief and non-chief gods and Asuras, he created the Sanasas, humans, and the great ancestors like fathers.
Lightning, thunderbolts, clouds, red Indra's bows, he made Riks, Yajus and Samans for the accomplishment of sacrifice.
High and low beings were born of his greatness. Brahma's creation of creatures — gods, sages, ancestors and humans —
again creates beings, moving and unmoving: Yakshas, Pishachas, Gandharvas, and everywhere Apsarases,
men, Kinnaras, Rakshasas, birds, beasts, deer and serpents; the imperishable and the perishable, the pair of unmoving and moving.
Their actions, created earlier by the Self-born, are those they follow; being created again and again they receive those same.
Violent and non-violent, mild and cruel, dharma and adharma, done and undone — of these the three, separate and undivided, they know.
This, thus, not so, neither of both, nor either — the sattva-abiding, equal-sighted, call this action's own domain.
Names of the self and the five elements, and the expansion of the created — by the word "heaven" Maheshvara made these five.
The sages' names and the creations among the gods are not born in the night; the lord established them again.
Thus the creation of the world by the Self-born came from cause; the transformations beginning with Mahat and ending with the specific are natural of themselves.
The world shines with moon and sun, adorned with planets and stars, with rivers, oceans and thousands of mountains,
with lovely cities of many kinds and prosperous countries. In this forest of Brahma the unmanifest Brahma, omniscient, roams.
Arising from the unmanifest seed, he stands only in his grace; made of the trunk of intellect, with the hollow of the senses within,
shining with the great elements, leafy with the specifics, with flowers of dharma and adharma, with the rising fruits of pleasure and pain,
the livelihood of all beings, the eternal tree of Brahma; this is the forest of Brahma, of that tree of Brahma.
Where the unmanifest cause is eternal, of nature of being and non-being, the thinkers on principles call it Pradhana, Prakriti, Maya.
Thus this path of grace is remembered as occasional to Brahma. Three creations of Brahma, natural, are without prior intellect.
The six creations beginning with the Sukhya are modified, with prior intellect; they proceed from variation of Brahma; they are his passions.
Thus these nine are remembered: natural and modified; the creations arise from one another; the wise remember the cause.
Whose head the Vedas declare, the sky his navel, the moon and sun his eyes; know the directions his ears and the earth his feet; he is of inconceivable self, leader of all beings.
From whose mouth Brahmins are born, from his chest in the front part Kshatriyas, Vaishyas from his thighs, and from his feet Shudras; all varnas are born from his body.
From Narayana, higher than the unmanifest, came the egg called unmanifest; Brahma himself, egg-born, himself made the worlds.
There, having stayed ten kalpas, they go again to Satya; those worlds are Brahma's world, a goal of no return.
Without sovereignty, they are equal to him in lordship; they become like Brahma in form and object.
There they remain, joined with joy, together with their own; by what must inevitably be, he himself spreads the natural.
Not connected with multiplicity, they are formed at that time, as when one asleep, without prior intent, has awareness.
Knowledge proceeds for them as formed at that time; by withdrawals of differences, not of the mighty.
With them proceed effects and causes, of those who see multiplicity, dwellers in Brahma's world,
whose modifications have ceased, standing in their own dharma, perfected with equal marks, of auspicious soul, stainless.
In the natural, endowed with instruments, established in their own self; having sent forth the self, Prakriti in truth...
Known by the plurality of other Purushas, she does not proceed; again the creation proceeds for those of cause-bearing nature.
Union is to be known as Prakriti, for those who see the truth; that is the release for those who go to no return burden.
Again, by non-existence, truly, like the peace of flames; when those glad-souled ones have gone upward from the three worlds,
together with them the Maharloka was then reached; their pupils who remain, when the burning of the kalpa arrives,
Gandharvas and others, Pishachas, humans, Brahmas and others, animals, birds, plants and reptiles —
while those dwelling on the earth's surface remain at that time, the thousand rays of the sun here are destroyed.
Those becoming seven rays, each one becomes a sun; in order, by hundreds, they burn the three worlds.
Moving and unmoving, all rivers and mountains, dried earlier by drought and heated by these (suns),
then all of them, helpless, are burned by the sun's rays, the moving and unmoving, of nature dharma and adharma.
With bodies burnt, then, their sins shaken off at the yuga's end, famed for their heat, freed by auspicious and strong bondage,
then they are born among people of equal form; having passed the night of Brahma, of unmanifest birth,
in the next creation the mind-born progeny of Brahma are here. Then, when the people living in the three worlds have gone into them,
the worlds being burnt by the seven suns, and then the earth being flooded by rain, with empty oceans,
the seas and clouds and waters and earthly things go, fugitive, named waters and mountains.
When much water came and went, covering this standing earth, it became the thing called the single ocean.
Because it shines (ābhāti), the syllable "bhā" is used for splendour and brilliance; all of it, attained, is distinguished by the radiance of months.
Because within it extends over the entire earth, from the root "tan" (to stretch) comes expansion, hence "bodies" are remembered.
Shara means shattered; the root is said to have many senses; in the single ocean the waters are not shattered, therefore those people...
When that thousand yugas ends and Brahma's day is complete, and the night of equal length proceeds, made of water,
then in that water, with the earth surface's fire extinguished, wind stilled, in darkness, everywhere without light,
the lord, Brahma's Purusha, by whom this is governed, wished again to make the division of this world.
Shara means shattered; the root is said to have many senses. Then in the single ocean, with the moving and unmoving lost, that Brahma becomes thousand-eyed, thousand-footed,
thousand-headed Purusha, golden-hued, beyond the senses. Brahma, named Narayana, then slept on the water.
Awakened by the rising of sattva, he saw the empty world. By this first quarter the Purana is proclaimed.
Animals, birds, plants and reptiles — while these remained at that time dwelling on the earth's surface,
the thousand rays of the sun appear of themselves; becoming seven rays, each one becomes a sun.
Rising in order, they burn the three worlds; moving and unmoving, all rivers and all mountains
are dried earlier by drought and fumigated by the suns; then all helpless ones are burned by the sun's rays,
the moving and unmoving, of nature dharma and adharma; with bodies burned, their sins shaken off at the yuga's end,
famed for heat, freed by auspicious and strong bondage, they then are born among people of equal form.
Having passed the night there of Brahma, of unmanifest birth, in the next creation Brahma's mind-born sons are here.
Then, when they have gone, with the people living in the three worlds, and the worlds being burnt by the seven suns,
the earth being flooded by rain, with empty oceans, the oceans' waters, clouds, and all earthly waters
go fugitive, named waters and followers. When that much water came and went,
covering this standing earth, it became called the single ocean. Because it shines (ābhāti) from its own radiance, the syllable "bhā" is for pervasion and brilliance;
by reaching all sides, their water is distinguished. Because within it stretches over the whole earth on all sides,
the root stretches in expansion, and these are not remembered as bodies. "Shara" means shattered; the root is said to have many senses;
in the single ocean the waters are not quick, therefore those people... When that thousand yugas ends and Brahma's day is complete,
and the night of equal length proceeds, made of water, then in that water, with the earth surface's fire extinguished,
wind stilled, darkness, everywhere without light — by this governed, Brahma, that Purusha, the lord,
wished again to make the division of this world. Then in the single ocean, with the moving and unmoving lost,
that Brahma becomes thousand-eyed, thousand-footed, thousand-headed Purusha, golden-hued, sense-conquered. They quote here this verse about Narayana:
The waters are 'nara', his bodies; so we have heard. Filling them he stays there; therefore he is remembered as Narayana.
Thousand-headed, good-minded, thousand-footed, thousand-eyed, thousand-faced, thousand-doing, thousand-armed, the first Prajapati, consisting of the three Vedas, this Purusha is called.
Sun-coloured, guardian of the world, alone formless, first, not different, Virat; Hiranyagarbha, the Purusha, great-souled, is beyond mind.
At the kalpa's beginning, pervaded by rajas, the lord became Brahma and created; at the kalpa's end, pervaded by tamas, becoming Time, he devoured again.
Becoming Narayana, pervaded by sattva, in the water's bed, dividing himself threefold he proceeds in the three worlds.
He creates, devours and is seen by himself threefold. Then in the single ocean, with the moving and unmoving lost,
at the end of a thousand caturyugas, when all is covered with water, Brahma named Narayana shone, himself existing.
All fourfold creatures, enveloped in darkness by Brahma's power, the great sages see him in Maharloka, Time asleep.

Bhrigu and others, as indicated, at that time, the great sages, and the eight beginning with Satya, when the kalpa dissolved, the great sages, then those turned around by them, the great and supreme...
The derivation of the word is said from the root "drish" (to go, to see): because it sees by sattva (it is) Mahat, therefore Maharshis.
By those staying in Maharloka Time was seen asleep then; the seven beginning with Sattva who were great sages in the past kalpa —
thus Brahma in those thousands of nights; the great sages brought saw Time asleep.
Because at a kalpa's beginning there are many fourteen stations, by arrangement Brahma (makes) months, therefore it is called kalpa.
He is the creator of all beings at the beginnings of kalpas again and again, manifest and unmanifest, the great god; his is all this world.
Thus the connection of the two kalpas has been told; the former state was between the two.
The former kalpa has been briefly told as it was; now I shall tell this kalpa; understand it.
With ramparts with openings, surrounded on all sides by moats; with a Ruchaka at each gate, and the maiden-city (Kumaripura),
of two cubits, the best of streams, the maiden-city... a hand-stream, ten best, and nine cubits.
Of khetas, cities, villages in all ways, and of the three kinds of forts — mountain, water, desert —
and of artificial forts, the width and length: a width of half a yojana, a length an eighth more,
the longest quarter-quarter in length, a city flooded eastward; with cut ears (?) and fan-like shape,
a round, vajra-shaped or long city is not praised; a divine city joined with a square is praised and made by them.
Twenty-four is the highest small measure, or one hundred and eight the highest of the site; here the middle is praised, the small without wood.
Then eight hundred kishkus is said to be the chief dwelling; a kheta is half the width of a city, and a pana above it.
From a city a yojana to a kheta, from a kheta half a yojana to a village; two krosha is the highest boundary, and the field boundary four bow-lengths.
A road of the directions, twenty bows wide, was made by them; a village road twenty bows, and boundary road just ten.
A glorious royal road, ten bows wide, was made; free of crowding for men, horses, chariots and elephants to move.
Four bows too were measured by them for branch lanes; the three-fold ones main and side streets, the two-fold side-of-side streets.
The shank-path is four feet, the space between houses three feet, the fence path six... and a footpath is remembered successively.
The scavenging surround is one foot on all sides. When those places had been made, houses and dwellings again —
as there had been trees earlier in the dwelling, so they began to make, thinking again and again.
Branches of the tree going this side, others going that, others going upward, others going crosswise —
having searched with intellect properly how the tree's branches went, as they made them, from "branches" (shakha) they are remembered as shalas.
Thus shalas and houses are famed from branches; therefore they are remembered as shalas; shala-hood is remembered in them.
Because (people) are pleased (prasidanti) in them, it is called prasada; therefore houses, shalas and prasadas are so named.
Having made opposites strike, they thought of means of relief; when the wishing trees were lost together with honey,
those created beings, agitated by despondency, were shown; then success arose for them in the Treta yuga.
Another accomplisher of all aims — rain — for them as desired; for them the rain water here which went sweet.
Thus the way proceeded in the second creation of rain: the drops of water beyond fell on the earth's surface;
from the union of water and earth, herbs then arose; herbs bearing flowers, roots and fruits were born.
Not ploughed or sown, fourteen village and wild (herbs) were delightful; trees and shrubs bearing flowers and fruit in season were born.
They appeared in Treta, by the maya of the herb; then the people lived on herbs in the beginning of Treta.
Then passion and greed arose again in them, always, by what must inevitably be and by the force of the Treta yuga.
Then they seized rivers, fields and mountains, trees, shrubs and herbs by force as each had strength.
Those perfected souls, earlier told to you in the Krita by me, who were Brahma's mind-born, born from the people here —
the peaceful, the mighty, the active and the suffering — returning then were born again in Treta.
Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, Shudras and the hostile folk, shaped in earlier births by the reputation of good and evil.
Then those strong ones who were truthful, non-violent, free of greed, self-conquered, lived among the remembered.
They made no acceptance (of property), speaking present; they did their works, and those who were weak for them
were in service, and others of less power than they. Thus, when they became opposed to one another and took refuge in each other,
by that fault the peaceful herbs vanished entirely then, like sand taken in fists.
Then by the strength of the yuga, the fourteen village and wild (herbs) take with fruits, flowers and roots again.
Then, when they were lost, those creatures were confused, all gripped by hunger, and they went to the Self-born.
Wishing a livelihood, in the beginning of Treta, the revered Self-born Brahma, knowing their thought,
reflecting with a vision seen directly of nourishment, knowing the herbs had been swallowed by the earth, made them rise again,
making Meru the calf, he milked this earth; this cow then (gave) seeds on the surface of the earth.
Those seeds were born, the village and wild plants; the lord made herbs ripen in fruit, subject to moments and sevens.
Rice, barley, wheat, chickpeas, sesame, priyangu, udara, koradusha with vamaka,
black gram, green gram, lentils, wild rice with horse-gram, harika and charaka: seventeen are remembered.
Thus are remembered the kinds of village herbs; shyamaka, nivara, jartila with gavedhuka,
kuruvinda, venuyava, mati and katakas are remembered; these are the fourteen village and wild herbs.
These arose at the beginning of the first Treta yuga; unploughed, all fourteen village and wild.
Trees, shrubs, creepers, climbers, grasses and kinds of plants, nourished with roots, fruits and shoots, they took whatever fruit.
The earth was milked of the seeds that the Self-born had before; those herbs bearing flowers and fruits in season were born here.
When the herbs created did not spread again here, then for their sustenance he devised the means of livelihood.
The revered Self-born gave them the hand-skill born of his own work; from then on herbs were born as ploughed and ripened.
Then, the body perfected in livelihood, Prajapati established for them a limit by which they protected one another.
Those who were the takers among them were stronger; he established the Kshatriyas, giving protection to the others.
